dek: The Sahyadris start just beyond Mumbai's suburbs and Pune sits right among them. Here are the best adventure weekends for both cities, with the right season for each.

intro: Mumbai and Pune share the same adventure playground: the forts, cliffs and plateaus of the Sahyadri range, the rivers that drop from them to the Konkan coast, and the coast itself. Most of the places below are two to four hours from either city, which makes day trips and one-night weekends easy.

Seasons matter more than distance here. The monsoon, from June to September, is peak time for treks and rafting at Kolad, while paragliding and beach water sports run in the dry months. We have merged Mumbai and Pune into one guide because the destinations are the same.
quickAnswer: The best weekend adventure trips from Mumbai and Pune are Kundalika river rafting at Kolad (best in the monsoon), paragliding at Kamshet (mid-October to May), Sahyadri treks such as Rajmachi, Lohagad, Harishchandragad and Kalsubai, lakeside camping at Pawna and Bhandardara, the bungee jump at Della Adventure near Lonavala, and water sports at Alibaug or, on a long weekend, Tarkarli.
takeaways: Kolad is about three hours from both cities; its dam-fed rapids are best in the monsoon.
Kamshet is Maharashtra's paragliding centre, flying from about mid-October to late May.
Sahyadri fort treks are greenest from June to September and drier from October to February.
Pawna Lake and Bhandardara are easy overnight camping trips.
Local authorities close risky waterfalls and fort paths in heavy rain; follow their orders.

items.name: Kundalika river rafting, Kolad
body: Rafting on the Kundalika depends on the morning water release from a hydroelectric project upstream, giving Grade II to III rapids that suit beginners. It is busiest and most exciting in the monsoon.

items.name: Alibaug water sports
body: Beaches near Alibaug have parasailing, jet skis and banana rides in the dry months, reached by ferry from Mumbai.

items.name: Tarkarli and Malvan (long weekend)
body: The Sindhudurg coast has try dives, snorkelling, parasailing and backwater boat rides, an overnight journey from either city.

items.name: Kamshet paragliding
body: Several schools run tandem flights and courses from Tower Hill and Shelar near Kamshet, between Lonavala and Pune.

items.name: Panchgani paragliding
body: Tandem flights over the Krishna valley near Panchgani and Mahabaleshwar in the dry season.

items.name: Bungee at Della Adventure, Lonavala
body: A jump of about 45 metres in an adventure park with many other activities.

items.name: Rajmachi
body: A long, gentle walk or a steeper climb to twin forts above Lonavala; famous for fireflies in May and early June.

items.name: Lohagad and Visapur
body: Two forts near Malavli station, easy first treks.

items.name: Harishchandragad
body: A plateau fort with caves, a temple and the Konkan Kada cliff; overnight treks are popular.

items.name: Kalsubai
body: Maharashtra's highest peak, at about 1,646 metres, with ladders on the steep sections.

items.name: Matheran
body: A car-free hill station with forest walks to viewpoints and, for the fit, the old footpath up from Neral.

items.name: Pawna Lake
body: Lakeside tent camps near Lonavala with bonfires and views of Tung and Tikona forts.

items.name: Bhandardara
body: Camps by Arthur Lake below Kalsubai and Ratangad; fireflies before the monsoon.

table.caption: Times are approximate and depend heavily on traffic.

sections.heading: Three sample weekends

items.name: Monsoon rafting and camping
body: Saturday: early start to Kolad, raft the morning release, afternoon river crossing or ziplining at a Kolad camp, and stay overnight. Sunday: short trek or waterfall visit where permitted, return.

items.name: Fly and camp
body: Saturday: tandem paragliding at Kamshet in the morning or evening slot, drive to Pawna Lake for a lakeside camp. Sunday: sunrise over the lake and a climb to Tikona or Lohagad.

items.name: A Sahyadri trek weekend
body: Saturday: overnight trek to Harishchandragad from Khireshwar, camping near the top. Sunday: sunrise at Konkan Kada and descend.

facts.Best time: October to February, or monsoon with care

after: From Mumbai, Friday-night departures via the expressway save time; from Pune, most of these are easy Saturday starts. Local trains and state buses reach Lonavala, Karjat and Kasara, the usual starting points for Sahyadri treks.

sections.heading: Weekend tips
list: For monsoon treks, leave early and avoid the most crowded weekends in July and August.
Local trains from Mumbai reach Lonavala, Malavli and Karjat, useful for day treks.
Book Kolad rafting and Kamshet flights ahead on weekends.
Check district orders; some forts, waterfalls and dams are closed in heavy rain.

safety: Avoid cliff edges, waterfalls and swollen streams in the monsoon; accidents happen every year.
Raft only with operators who give a safety briefing, life jackets and helmets.
Fly with registered paragliding schools and accept weather cancellations.
Carry a torch; monsoon treks get dark early under cloud.
Do not trek alone on less-used Sahyadri routes.

faqs.q: What are the best adventure activities near Mumbai?
faqs.a: Kolad rafting, Kamshet paragliding, Sahyadri treks such as Rajmachi and Harishchandragad, Pawna Lake camping and the Lonavala bungee.
In the monsoon, from about June to September, when the rapids are strongest.

faqs.q: When is the paragliding season at Kamshet?
faqs.a: From about mid-October to late May.

faqs.q: Which is the best monsoon trek near Pune?
faqs.a: Rajmachi, Lohagad, Harishchandragad and Kalsubai are popular; choose by fitness.

faqs.q: Can I go scuba diving near Mumbai?
faqs.a: The nearest regular dive sites are at Tarkarli and Malvan on the Sindhudurg coast, an overnight journey away.
